paragraphs: Friend, this passage is HEAVY, so I'm going to say it plain. The LORD hands Jeremiah a cup, and every nation on that long list has to drink it, with no exceptions (Jeremiah 25:17-26). Even when a nation refuses, the LORD says, "You most certainly must drink it!" (Jeremiah 25:28). I think the first thing this teaches us is that God is serious about sin, and nobody gets to sit this one out.

Now look at where He starts. He says, "I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears My Name, so how could you possibly go unpunished?" (Jeremiah 25:29). The people who carried His Name were first in line, and Jeremiah had been warning them for twenty-three years (Jeremiah 25:3). That should make every one of us stop and listen when God speaks, because carrying His Name never meant we could ignore Him.

So here's what I'm taking to the bakery today. The LORD roars, and He is not whispering for fun (Jeremiah 25:30). He brings a charge against the nations because He is just, and a warning is a kindness when it comes early. I'm so glad I get to bake for the Supper of the Lamb, friend, and I want to hear His Word the first time, not the twenty-third year.
